question: How many milliseconds does each steady-yellow and steady-red stage last in Figure 4J-3?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 4J-3 does not specify any durations in milliseconds (or seconds) — it only shows the sequence of displays for a pedestrian hybrid beacon. The only timing information in the evidence is Guidance that the steady yellow change interval should last 3 to 6 seconds (i.e., 3,000–6,000 milliseconds); no duration is given for the steady-red pedestrian walk interval, which depends on local signal timing. Standards (mandatory): - "Following an actuation by a pedestrian, a pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall display a flashing CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by a steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian walk interval, followed by alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian change interval (see Figure 4J-3)." (This sets the sequence, not the durations.) Guidance (recommended): - "A steady yellow change interval should have a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 6 seconds (see Section 4F.17). The longer intervals should be reserved for use on approaches with higher speeds." (Equivalent to 3,000–6,000 ms.) Options (permitted): - "A steady red clearance interval may be used after the steady yellow change interval." (No duration is specified in the evidence.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4J-3 shows the six-interval sequence (dark, flashing yellow, steady yellow, steady red during walk, alternating flashing red, dark again) with a note about optional steady red clearance and buffer intervals, but no timing values. [Image 7] shows the same figure with the surrounding text of Section 4J.03, which likewise contains no millisecond durations. Citations: - Section 4J.03 Standard §2 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Guidance §11 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Option §12 (p.730) - Figure 4J-3 (p.729) - Page 730
